title: jit commands fail from any subdirectory instead of discovering the repo root like git
description:
`jit` only looks for a `.jit/` directory in the current working directory. Run from any subdirectory of the repository it aborts with "JIT repository not found", even though a valid repository exists in an ancestor directory. Git discovers its repository root by walking up parent directories; jit should do the same.

## Background

Observed 2026-07-05 in a checked-out repository whose root contains `.jit/`:

```
$ cd crates/jit/src && jit status
Error: JIT repository not found at '.../crates/jit/src/.jit'
Initialize a repository with: jit init

$ cd .jit/issues && jit status
Error: JIT repository not found at '.../.jit/issues/.jit'
```

The same commands succeed from the repository root. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` succeeds from every one of those directories, because git ascends until it finds `.git`.

Two distinct problems:

1. **No upward discovery.** jit resolves the data directory as `<cwd>/.jit` with no parent traversal, so every invocation must run from the exact repository root.
2. **Misleading remedy.** The error tells the user to run `jit init` or set an override, implying no repository exists. The real cause is that a repository exists in an ancestor the resolver never checked; following the suggestion would create a nested repository in the wrong place.

The `.jit/issues` case is the sharpest: standing inside the repository's own internals reports the repository as absent.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: a command run from any subdirectory of a repository resolves the repository rooted at the nearest ancestor of the current directory that contains `.jit/`, verified from at least one source subdirectory and from inside `.jit/` itself.
- [hard] REQ-02: discovery stops at a `.git` boundary — if no `.jit/` is found in the current directory or any ancestor up to and including the directory containing `.git`, discovery halts there rather than escaping into a parent directory's unrelated `.jit/`.
- [hard] REQ-03: when no ancestor within the boundary contains `.jit/`, the "not found" error is still emitted and still suggests initialization.
- [hard] REQ-04: an explicit data-directory override, when set, takes precedence over ancestor discovery.
- [hard] REQ-05: discovery terminates at the filesystem root without unbounded traversal.

## Notes

Mirror git's algorithm: start at cwd, ascend parent by parent, stop at the first directory containing `.jit/`, and do not cross the `.git` boundary or the filesystem root. The override path must be checked ahead of discovery.
